28.0.s.en: 1. Prophecy against the prince of Tyre:

28.0.0.en: 1 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 2 "Son of man, say unto the prince of Tyrus, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God, I sit in the seat of God, in the midst of the seas; yet thou art a man, and not God, though thou set thine heart as the heart of God: 3 Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee: 4 With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures: 5 By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches, and thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches: 6 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; 7 Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness. 8 They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas. 9 Wilt thou yet say before him that slayeth thee, I am God? but thou shalt be a man, and no God, in the hand of him that slayeth thee. 10 Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD." 11 Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 12 "Son of man, take up a lamentation upon the king of Tyrus, and say unto him, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty. 13 Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the sapphire, the emerald, and the carbuncle, and gold: the workmanship of thy settings and of thy engravings was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created. 14 Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God; thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire. 15 Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee. 16 By the multitude of thy merchandise they have filled the midst of thee with violence, and thou hast sinned: therefore I will cast thee out of the mountain of God: and I will destroy thee, O covering cherub, from the midst of the stones of fire. 17 Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty, thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness: I will cast thee to the ground, I will lay thee before kings, that they may behold thee. 18 Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee. 19 All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never shalt thou be any more."

28.0.1.en: St. Jerome sees that the word "Tyre" means "distress." Therefore what is said about the prince or king of Tyre is meant of Satan, since he drives people into distresses and trials. Many of the Fathers saw that what is said in this chapter describes the fall of Satan from his angelic rank. This description corresponds to what is said about Lucifer in (Isa 14:12).

28.0.2.en: It is noticed in this chapter that the prince or king of Tyre is described as a good creature of God, indeed a perfect one, because Satan was not created evil; he is a good creature of God who fell through pride, by his own free will.

28.0.4.en: "Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty.

28.0.5.en: Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God.

28.0.6.en: Every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius... the workmanship of thy settings was prepared in thee in the day that thou wast created.

28.0.7.en: Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God.

28.0.8.en: Thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire.

28.1.0.en: Thou wast perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee" [12-15].

28.1.1.en: Satan was one of the greatest and mightiest of the heavenly orders, the order of the Cherubim who bear the divine throne, aflame with fire like a divine chariot of fire! He was the seal of perfection, because he bore the throne; full of wisdom, for we know that the cherub is full of eyes; perfect in beauty, for he reflects the splendor of God upon himself. He was adorned with every precious stone, for God lacked him nothing; he covered with his wings upon the holy mountain of God, and wherever he was found he proclaimed the presence of God, who sanctifies all things. He walked among the stones of fire, a sign of the fiery divine presence. He was created without blemish, perfect in all his ways.

28.1.2.en: It is clear that the discourse here does not apply to man, the most perfect of God's creatures on earth, nor to any heavenly order, but to the greatest and loftiest of the orders... Tertullian says: [If we return to the prophecy of Ezekiel, we find that this angel was good by his creation but corrupted himself by his own choice. For in the person of the king of Tyre it was said of Satan: "Thou sealest up the sum... etc." And it is clear that this description [11-16] concerns the rebellion of the angel and not the prince of Tyre, for among human beings there is none who was born in the paradise of God (even Adam himself was only brought into it), and there is no one who is a cherub placed upon the holy mountain of God, that is, in the heights of heaven, except the one of whom the Lord testified that from there he fell (Lk 10:18)].

28.1.3.en: Origen of Alexandria speaks of Satan and his angels as a good creation that sinned by its own will, saying: [Those who say that Satan is not the creation of God are mistaken. For insofar as he is Satan, he is not the creation of God, but the being himself (as a creature) is the creation of God. It is like saying that a murderer is not the creation of God, but as a man he is the creation of God].

28.1.4.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [(Satan) did not sin by compulsion, as though there were in him a natural inclination to sin; otherwise the cause of sin would return to his Creator as well. Rather, he is a good creature, and by his free will he became the devil, receiving the name through his work. He was an archangel, but he was called "the devil" because of his deceptions. He was a good servant of God, and he became truly Satan. For "Satan" means "the adversary." This teaching is not of my own; it is the teaching of the inspired prophet Ezekiel, who raised a lamentation over him, saying: "Thou wast the seal of the likeness of God, the crown of splendor, born in paradise," and then he says again: "Thou walkedst perfect in thy ways from the day that thou wast created, till iniquity was found in thee." He rightly said, "till iniquity was found in thee," for iniquity did not come to him from outside, but he brought it upon himself. And immediately he points to the cause, saying: "Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty. By reason of the multitude of thy sins thou wast wounded and cast to the ground." This saying agrees with the word of the Lord in the Gospel: "I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven" (Lk 10:18)].

28.1.5.en: In raising a lamentation over Satan, He proclaims God's gifts to him and the capacities that were granted to him on the day He created him. For to the degree that much was given him, much is required of him, and to the degree that he enjoyed a towering height, his fall became great. The most important of the divine gifts to him are:

28.1.6.en: a. The gift of wisdom: "Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel; there is no secret that they can hide from thee" [3]. He gave him wisdom, so he was wiser than the prophet Daniel, to whom were revealed the secrets of the king, his personal dreams and their interpretations, to support him in his exile. It is as though God, in His dealings with Satan before his fall, revealed many secrets to him, so that He said: "There is no secret that they can hide from thee." He dealt with him as a trusted friend and a man of confidence, and hid no secret from him, saying to him: "Thou sealest up the sum, full of wisdom, and perfect in beauty" [12]. He made him the most perfect and most beautiful of His heavenly creatures, not in appearance but in wisdom; yet when he fell into pride, he fell from this height into the abyss!

28.1.7.en: Man too is the most perfect of God's creatures on earth. God adorned him not with the beauty of the body but with what is greater: the beauty of wisdom, since He created him "in His image and likeness" and wanted him to be a master who rules over the earthly creation with the spirit of divine wisdom. As pride brought the angel down to become a Satan, so pride brought man down to a corrupt, sensual nature and made him, in many matters, behave as lower than the animals, even the beasts of prey.

28.2.0.en: b. His dwelling in the garden of God: "Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God" [13]. The word Eden means "delight," as though He set him in the divine joy, enjoying the divine presence, and even sharing with the rest of the Cherubim in bearing the divine throne; and he came to an inward torment that has no end.

28.2.1.en: Man too was set by God in the garden of Eden to work and to rejoice, and by his pride he lost his true paradise and deprived himself of God, the source of joy. Therefore, for the repair of our nature it was necessary that we be planted anew in God, so that we become like those who are in the eternal paradise... For this reason St. Cyril of Jerusalem addresses those approaching Baptism thus: [Soon paradise will be opened to each one of you], for they enter into union with God in Christ Jesus, the true paradise.

28.2.2.en: c. The gift of work: The Lord Christ says, "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work" (Jn 5:17). It is the characteristic of God, who works without ceasing, and He gave it to the rational creation so that it might work continually. But Satan worked not for the glory of his Creator but for the account of his own glory, so his work became not for his edification but for his destruction. "With thy wisdom and with thine understanding thou hast gotten thee riches, and hast gotten gold and silver into thy treasures. By thy great wisdom and by thy traffick hast thou increased thy riches" [4-5]. In this God rejoices, for He desires to see the treasuries of His creation always filled with every precious wealth and riches, but what grieved Him was this: "thine heart is lifted up because of thy riches" [5]. Riches are a blessing and a grace, but the lifting up of the heart corrupts the heart of the rich man, so that he thinks himself a god: "Because thou hast set thine heart as the heart of God; behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee, the terrible of the nations: and they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom, and they shall defile thy brightness. They shall bring thee down to the pit, and thou shalt die the deaths of them that are slain in the midst of the seas" [6-8]. What befalls him is not because of his wisdom, nor his beauty, nor his riches, but because of the pride of his heart; he thought himself a god, so he was deprived of his wisdom, his beauty, his riches, and life itself.

28.2.3.en: The Fathers spoke much about work and its importance, and about riches and their blessings... declaring that it is pride that corrupts work and riches. St. Clement of Alexandria wrote a book on this subject, entitled "Who Is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved?", in which he says: "We do not cast the rich man to the ground, he who benefits our brethren... A man does not squander his riches, but rather it is fitting for him to break down his inward passions that conflict with the good use of riches. For when a man becomes virtuous and good, he can use these riches in a good way. Let us therefore understand the leaving and selling of our kingdoms (Mk 10:13-17) to mean a leaving and selling of the passions of our souls."

28.2.4.en: d. He gave every precious stone [13]: The Septuagint gives the same twelve stones that were placed on the breastplate of the high priest, and with which the wall of the heavenly Jerusalem was adorned (Rev 21:19-20). They point to the divine virtues and the gifts with which God adorns the soul, so that it may enter His sanctuaries radiant and shining. For this reason the Lord comforts His struggling Church, saying to her: "O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones... This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD" (Isa 54:11-17). God adorns His rational creation with gifts and virtues... but when it falls into pride, it becomes a cause of judgment against it!

28.3.0.en: e. The fiery nature: "Thou art the anointed cherub that covereth; and I have set thee so: thou wast upon the holy mountain of God" [14]. He set him with a fiery nature, a blazing cherub, and made him dwell in the sanctuaries, so he became without excuse. God has given us the capacities of the new nature and planted us in Him, "the holy mountain," so we have become without excuse before Him.

28.4.0.en: f. "Thou hast walked up and down in the midst of the stones of fire" [16], for he was like a cherub walking among the Cherubim and Seraphim who blaze with fire. He ought to have remained like them, a holy fire, and not to fall from among them. So the Cherubim condemn Satan, because he was with them and fell! And the Apostles also will judge the twelve tribes of Israel, because they were Jews and accepted the faith, whereas the Jews rejected faith in Christ, the mystery of the sanctification and salvation of mankind!

28.5.0.en: Pride makes the creature a god in his own eyes: "Thine heart is lifted up, and thou hast said, I am a God" [2]. Therefore it brings him down to die the most hideous death: "Thou shalt die the deaths of the uncircumcised by the hand of strangers: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD" [10]. The Phoenicians practiced circumcision, and considered that one who dies uncircumcised is despised and in great shame! Thus pride does not only kill him, but also puts him in great shame!

28.5.1.en: As for the place of the slaying, according to the Septuagint, "I will cut thee off (cast thee) as one slain from the mountain of God" [16]. St. Jerome clarifies for us this mountain of God on which the king of Tyre was slain, saying: [The mountain of God is rich in its blessings (Ps 86:16); this is the mountain mentioned by Ezekiel, on which the king of Tyre was punished].

28.5.2.en: [(The mountain) points to the presence of the Savior who became flesh, for in Him the divine nature dwelt. Truly, there is no other way in which the Holy Spirit found His dwelling immediately and continually except in the Savior, and as John says: "Upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining on him, the same is he" (Jn 1:33), "the LORD will dwell in it for ever" (Ps 68:16), in the body which He took from the blessed Mary]. Through this holy mountain Satan was wounded, since he found no place in it; through the Lord Christ Satan was driven out from mankind.

28.6.0.en: 20 Again the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 21 "Son of man, set thy face against Zidon, and prophesy against it, 22 And say, Thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I am against thee, O Zidon; and I will be glorified in the midst of thee: and they shall know that I am the LORD, when I shall have executed judgments in her, and shall be sanctified in her. 23 For I will send into her pestilence, and blood into her streets; and the wounded shall be judged in the midst of her by the sword upon her on every side; and they shall know that I am the LORD. 24 And there shall be no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel, nor any grieving thorn of all that are round about them, that despised them; and they shall know that I am the Lord GOD. 25 Thus saith the Lord GOD; When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob. 26 And they shall dwell safely therein, and shall build houses, and plant vineyards; yea, they shall dwell with confidence, when I have executed judgments upon all those that despise them round about them; and they shall know that I am the LORD their God."

28.6.1.en: We have already spoken of Zidon as the "land of hunting." She shared with Tyre in mocking Judah over its captivity, and became a pricking brier and a grieving thorn. Since she embittered the life of the children of God, He sends pestilence upon her to be a painful thorn to her.

28.6.2.en: Finally He makes clear that He does all this in order to gather His scattered people and sanctify His name in them, to satisfy them with good things and grant them peace! This is God's continual longing, to see mankind return to rest in Him, and be satisfied and filled with peace as a holy bride to Him.

28.6.4.en: * Satan has become a lesson to me!

28.6.5.en: You created him among the Cherubim, perfect and full of wisdom and beauty!

28.6.6.en: He knows many of Your divine secrets!

28.6.7.en: But through pride he collapsed from heaven to the abyss!

28.6.8.en: You made me the most wonderful of Your creatures on earth, You granted me mind, wisdom, and beauty!

28.6.9.en: Grant me the spirit of humility, that I may cling to You, and enjoy the splendor of Your beauty upon me!

28.6.10.en: * You set him in heaven, rejoicing and exulting in Your presence; by his stubbornness he collapsed into eternal torment!

28.6.11.en: You set me in the garden of Eden to work and to praise!

28.6.12.en: When will You lift me up to Your paradise, to enjoy eternal glory?!

28.6.13.en: * God gave him riches, and his heart was lifted up by his riches!

28.6.14.en: You have not left me in want of the works of Your honor!

28.6.15.en: When shall I possess You, my treasure and my wealth!

28.6.16.en: You are my love! You are my praise!

28.6.17.en: You are my joy and the exultation of my heart!

28.6.18.en: You are my satisfaction and my wealth!

28.6.20.en: * You adorned him with every precious stone; by his disobedience he became ugly, deprived of everything beautiful and precious!

28.6.21.en: You adorned me with gifts like precious stones; kindle in me Your gifts as a precious inheritance!

28.6.22.en: * You created him a fiery cherub, You made him dwell in the sanctuaries, and by his own will he collapsed to dwell in an eternal fire that is never quenched!

28.6.23.en: You renewed me by Your fiery Holy Spirit, to carry me to the throne of Your glory, to a light that none can approach!

28.6.24.en: When shall I become like the cherub, and like a servant of light!

28.6.25.en: I await Your coming, O true Light!
